questions.title: Checkpoint granularity
questions.context: The pipeline has these logical phases: train -> encode_clean (per task) -> attack (per task) -> evaluate (per task) -> analysis. Currently only training has reuse via `reuse_trained_checkpoint` flag (core.py:198). There can be multiple downstream tasks per run.

options.label: Coarse-grained (5 phases)
options.description: Track: training, encoding, attacks, evaluation, analysis. Simple state file, fewer I/O operations. If encoding for task 2 of 3 fails, restarts encoding all tasks — but encoding is the cheapest phase anyway.

options.label: Per-task granularity (Recommended)
options.description: Track completion per (step, task_name) pair. E.g., {'encoding': ['classification'], 'attacks': ['classification']}. More precise recovery with minimal complexity cost. State file is still a small JSON.

options.label: Checkpoint on exit, never partial
options.description: No step-level state. On crash, always restart from beginning but reuse existing artifacts (checkpoint file, representation NPZs). Simpler to implement but wastes time re-encoding.

questions.title: State file location and format
questions.context: The run directory is `output_dir/run_name/` (config.py:224-226). Current artifacts go into `checkpoints/`, `representations/`, `metrics/`, `analysis/`. The state file needs to survive interruptions.

options.label: Inside run directory (Recommended)
options.description: `run_dir/.pipeline_state.json` — self-contained, travels with the run. Hidden file so it doesn't clutter `ls`. Contains: steps_completed dict, timestamps, config hash for integrity verification.

options.label: Alongside checkpoint
options.description: `run_dir/checkpoints/.pipeline_state.json` — colocated with model weights. Makes sense if state is tightly coupled to checkpoint identity.

options.label: Project-level state registry
options.description: `output_dir/.pipeline_registry.json` — tracks all runs globally. Overkill for this use case but enables cross-run queries.

questions.title: Run directory hierarchy
questions.context: Current: `output_dir/{experiment_id}_{dataset_name}/`. Reference (autotsaugment): `output_dir/{hashed_experiment_folder}/seed_{seed}/{dataset_name}/`. The reference structure shares experiment folder across datasets and seeds. Currently each run is a flat directory.

options.label: Keep flat, improve naming (Recommended)
options.description: `output_dir/{experiment_id}/seed_{seed}/{dataset_name}/` — hierarchical but readable. Experiment artifacts are grouped by ID, then seed, then dataset. Deterministic and human-scannable.

options.label: Reference-style with hash
options.description: Adopt autotsaugment pattern: hash-based experiment folder. Guarantees uniqueness but hurts readability. Useful when same experiment config is slightly perturbed.

options.label: Minimal change — add seed to path
options.description: `output_dir/{experiment_id}_{dataset_name}_seed{seed}/` — adds seed disambiguation to existing flat structure. Lowest change, but doesn't group runs by experiment.

questions.title: Experiment metadata files
questions.context: The reference runner saves metadata at run start. Currently `results_summary.json` is written at the very end (core.py:170-179), which means crashed runs lose their config.

options.label: Config at start, summary at end (Recommended)
options.description: Write `experiment_config.json` at run start (model params, attack params, seed, dataset, trainer kwargs). Write `results_summary.json` at end with metrics. Crash-safe config means you can always reconstruct what was attempted.

options.label: Single consolidated file at end
options.description: One `run_manifest.json` at the end with config + results + timing. Simpler but requires the state file to preserve config for crash reconstruction.

options.label: Config at start, incremental updates
options.description: Write config at start, append results/analysis as each phase completes. Most crash-resilient but file grows over time.

questions.title: Dataset selection for HPC compatibility
questions.context: Current runner uses `--dataset_name` (string). The reference uses `--dataset_index` (integer) with SLURM array `$SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID`. HPC array jobs need integer indices to look up dataset names from a registry. A `get_all_datasets()` equivalent exists in `data_setup.py`.

options.label: Add --dataset_index, deprecate --dataset_name (Recommended)
options.description: Primary interface: `--dataset_index` for HPC. Keep `--dataset_name` as a convenience alias for local testing. Mutually exclusive. Maps index to name via dataset registry.

options.label: Both first-class, auto-detect
options.description: Accept both, require exactly one. `if dataset_index: name = registry[index]` elif dataset_name: use directly. No deprecation — both are equally valid.

options.label: Keep --dataset_name only
options.description: HPC scripts pass names directly. Works but requires the SLURM script to build a name array from indices. Extra indirection in the bash layer.

questions.title: Progress logging and structure
questions.context: Current runner prints a summary then 'Running experiment...' with no intermediate feedback. The pipeline can run hours on large datasets. tqdm is already used inside `encode()` and `_compute_sliding_representations()`. No structured logging exists.

options.label: Structured logging with tqdm (Recommended)
options.description: Use Python's `logging` module with INFO-level step transitions ('Starting training...', 'Training complete, checkpoint at...', 'Encoding clean representations for classification...'). Keep tqdm for inner loops. Logs to both stdout and `run_dir/experiment.log`.

options.label: Human-readable progress only
options.description: Print formatted progress to stdout with timestamps. No logging module, no log files. Simple but less queryable.

options.label: JSON-structured logging
options.description: Every step emits a JSON line. Machine-parseable but noisy for human readers. Good for CI/CD pipelines, overkill for research code.

questions.title: Resume flag behavior
questions.context: The `reuse_trained_checkpoint` flag (config.py:147) only affects training. A general resume mechanism needs a clear trigger. Should resume be opt-in or automatic?

options.label: Automatic resume (Recommended)
options.description: If `.pipeline_state.json` exists in the run directory, pipeline automatically resumes from last completed step. `--force` flag to override and start fresh. This is the HPC-friendly default — crashed jobs just continue.

options.label: Explicit --resume flag
options.description: Resume is opt-in via `--resume`. Safer for local development where you want clean runs, but requires HPC scripts to always pass the flag.

options.label: Auto-resume encoding+, explicit for training
options.description: Always reuse existing checkpoint and representations if found. Only training requires explicit `--resume`. Hybrid approach.

questions.title: Failure recovery policy
questions.context: When a step fails mid-pipeline (e.g., OOM during encoding, attack crashes), the state file may be incomplete. The reference runner has no recovery — SLURM just kills the job.

options.label: Atomic state writes with crash recovery (Recommended)
options.description: Write state to `.pipeline_state.json.tmp` then rename (atomic on POSIX). On resume, verify state file integrity with config hash. Failed steps are simply not marked complete — they re-run on next invocation.

options.label: Write state on success, clear on failure
options.description: Clear state file when any step fails. Forces full restart. Simple but defeats the purpose of resume for flaky steps.

options.label: State + retry with backoff
options.description: On step failure, retry N times with exponential backoff before giving up. Adds complexity but handles transient failures (network, GPU memory fragmentation).

questions.title: Unique filename generation
questions.context: The reference uses SHA-256 hashes of serialized model params to generate unique experiment folder names (autotsaugment runner.py:64-95). This guarantees uniqueness across parameter combinations but produces unreadable folder names like `b1_ts2vec_crop-shift_compNo_a3f2b7...`.

options.label: Named experiment IDs only (Recommended)
options.description: Use `experiment_id` from the registry as the unique identifier. No hashing — the registry guarantees uniqueness. Folder names are human-readable: `ts2vec_fgsm`, `autotcl_pgd`.

options.label: Short hash appendix
options.description: `{experiment_id}_{short_hash}` where hash is first 8 chars of SHA-256 of model params. Catches parameter drift while staying readable.

options.label: Full reference-style hashing
options.description: Adopt the autotsaugment approach: full hash of model + augmentation params. Maximum safety against parameter collisions but verbose.
